notes.label: Hours to a first merged PR
notes.text: Each skill needs a planning estimate of learn, practice and build hours before its first merged PR (rung 2 of the Proof Ladder), from 4 hours for Git to 24 for deep learning. Every future draws its own 0.8 to 1.4 times that, because skills usually take longer than planned.

notes.label: Weeks rarely go to plan
notes.text: Each simulated week delivers 60 to 100% of the hours you plan. People reliably underestimate how long their own work takes (the planning fallacy).
notes.source: Buehler, Griffin and Ross (1994), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 67(3)

notes.label: Demand keeps moving
notes.text: Each skill's share of job ads moves with the Trend Forecaster's 12-month projection, sampled inside its 95% prediction band, so readiness can change even in weeks you don't study.
notes.source: Trend Forecaster: OLS on logit share of Hacker News Who is hiring posts

notes.label: The Roadmap Agent's rules
notes.text: Exam weeks get half your hours. A skill started before its prerequisites are covered takes 1 / 0.6 as long, the same 0.6 the Roadmap Agent uses to rank it. Degree skills count as done when their module's term ends.

notes.label: Summer placement
notes.text: A 10-week placement from 21 June replaces self-study with about 6 hours a week of on-the-job learning on your next roadmap skill, and turns communication and teamwork into proven skills when it ends.
